item.title: Draft ministerial ordinance to preserve machinery-safety protections for interns and volunteers
item.description: AI summary: The Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare published a draft ministerial ordinance on 2026-11-20 to amend Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare Ordinance No. 29 of 2026, concerning implementation of amendments to the Industrial Safety and Health Act and the Working Environment Measurement Act. The draft would retain an employer duty under Article 27 of the Ordinance on Industrial Safety and Health to prevent use of machinery lacking prescribed standards or safety devices, excluding cases covered by Article 42(2) and (3) of the Industrial Safety and Health Act (Act No. 57 of 1972). The explanatory excerpt identifies a potential protection gap arising from the earlier deletion of Article 27 for people who are neither workers nor covered working officers or sole proprietors, such as interns and volunteers. The stated comment deadline is 2026-12-19 15:00 JST. Promulgation is planned for late February 2027, with commencement on the promulgation date. item.title: Draft maritime radio amendments: AMRD, fishing-vessel equipment and four-digit VHF channels
item.description: AI summary: The Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications published draft Ministerial Ordinance and related amendments for public comment on 2026-11-21, with a stated deadline of 2026-12-21 at 23:59 JST. The proposals would amend existing radio-station standards and related instruments to introduce Autonomous Maritime Radio Devices (AMRD), which use AIS technology to assist person-overboard rescue and the detection, location and avoidance of fishing gear. They would also reflect radio-equipment quantities for qualifying fishing vessels under the Cape Town Agreement, which the announcement says is expected to enter into force on 2027-02-24. Related notice amendments would support four-digit international VHF channels; the announcement cites an IMO circular specifying adaptation by the first radio-station inspection on or after 2028-01-01. The excerpts do not establish a commencement date for the proposed domestic amendments. item.title: Draft Notice to Add Locker and Designated-Location Delivery to Standard Parcel Delivery Terms
item.description: AI summary: The Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism published a draft amending Notice for public comment on 2026-11-20, with a stated deadline of 2026-12-11 23:59 JST. It would amend the Standard Parcel Delivery Terms and Conditions (Ministry of Transport Notice No. 576 of 1990), established under Article 10(3) of the Motor Truck Transportation Business Act (Act No. 83 of 1989), which the explanatory text says presently provides only for face-to-face handover. Proposed Article 11(2) would allow delivery by a sender- or recipient-designated method, including secure parcel lockers or an appropriate recipient-designated location, to count as handover to the recipient; sender designation would require agreement with the recipient, and delivery would require written or electronic notification to the recipient. Promulgation is planned for mid-December 2026, with proposed commencement on 2027-04-01. Contracts concluded before commencement would remain subject to the previous terms. item.title: Draft Cabinet Order to raise hazardous-materials and fire-equipment training fees
item.description: AI summary: A draft Cabinet Order would raise fees for training provided by designated examination bodies: from JPY 5,300 to JPY 6,000 for safety training on hazardous-materials handling, and from JPY 7,000 to JPY 7,800 for training on installation or maintenance of covered fire-service equipment. It would amend Article 40(2) of the Cabinet Order on the Control of Hazardous Materials (Cabinet Order No. 306 of 1959) and Article 36-8 of the Order for Enforcement of the Fire Service Act (Cabinet Order No. 37 of 1961), under the Fire Service Act (Act No. 186 of 1948). The proposed effective date is April 1, 2027. The Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications' Fire and Disaster Management Agency published the public-comment listing on November 21, 2026; the stated deadline was December 21, 2026, at 23:59 JST, with postal submissions also required to arrive by the deadline. item.title: Draft ministerial ordinance and notices on maritime radio stations and equipment
item.description: AI summary: The Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications announced a public consultation on 2026-11-20 on a draft ministerial ordinance amending the Fundamental Standards for Establishing Radio Stations (excluding basic broadcasting stations) and related rules. The draft Article 5 would expand permitted communication counterparts for fisheries coast stations to include radio stations aboard non-fishing vessels, while retaining a condition that communications concern the specified persons' fishing activities and be minimal. The package would amend seven ordinances, the Frequency Assignment Plan and related notices, and introduce a new notice establishing technical conditions for autonomous maritime radio equipment. Other listed subjects include ship and aircraft station frequency symbols, distress-alert station equipment testing, ship earth stations and digital selective calling equipment for ship and coast stations. The excerpts do not establish a comment deadline, commencement date or the detailed technical changes across the full package. item.title: MIC publishes FY2026 telecom consumer-protection monitoring plan and public-comment results
item.description: AI summary: On 2026-11-20, the Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications (MIC) published its FY2026 consumer-protection monitoring survey plan and results of public consultation held from 2026-08-25 to 2026-09-24, which received 22 submissions. The plan covers mobile network operator (MNO), mobile virtual network operator (MVNO), fiber-to-the-home (FTTH), standalone ISP and cable television internet services, excluding contracts not subject to explanation duties and services primarily involving machine-to-machine communications. It provides for industry-association interviews across all five service categories, with additional provider and sales-agent interviews, mystery shopping and user questionnaires for MNO, MVNO and FTTH services. Survey topics include explanations of service terms, delivery of contract documents, initial contract cancellation arrangements and complaint handling; this is a monitoring plan, not an announcement of newly enacted obligations. item.title: MLIT announces data leak in Building Standards Act structural-method approval system
item.description: AI summary: On 2026-11-20, the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism (MLIT) announced that unauthorized external manipulation had caused information to leak from its system for applications and certificates for ministerial approval of structural methods and building materials under the Building Standards Act. The identified leak comprised six cases involving applicant information, including corporate representatives' names and positions and contact persons' names, departments and work telephone numbers, and 18 cases involving application content, including outlines of structural methods and building materials. At the time of the announcement, MLIT had suspended the system and blocked all external access while investigating the cause; it planned to resume operation after implementing preventive measures. MLIT reported that applications were being handled outside the system and asked affected applicants to contact it about suspicious communications or other unusual events. Original title: 建築基準法に基づく「構造方法等の認定」の申請を行うシステムにおける申請に関する図書情報の漏洩について Government Announcement | Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism (MLIT) | Published 2026-11-20 | First detected 2026-11-21 Monitoring aid only; not legal advice or an official translation.
